:::{#exm-complex-vector}
#### A complex vector and its conjugate

$$
\underbrace{\vecf{z}}_{3 \times 1} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 + i \\ 2 \\ -3\,i \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{C}^3,
\qquad
\underbrace{\overline{\vecf{z}}}_{3 \times 1} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 - i \\ 2 \\ 3\,i \end{bmatrix}.
$$

The real entry $2$ is its own conjugate.
Every real vector is also a complex vector,
since each real number $a$ is the complex number $a + 0\,i$,
so $\reals^p$ is a subset of $\mathbb{C}^p$.

:::
